rewrites.summary: Inland Black Sea province, conservative province; no province-specific trans-related findings were located in this research pass, so the national framework and its 2025–26 escalation apply here unchanged: what a trans visitor in Karabük stands under is the same national framework that binds every province, and the region's own sources are national-level. A leaked draft omnibus reform package (the '11th Judicial Package', October 2025) would create new anti-LGBT articles, criminalising conduct deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' (up to three years in prison), participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies (up to four years — same-sex marriage is not legal, so such ceremonies are symbolic, which bears on travelling with a partner), and restricting gender-affirming healthcare including surgery to people aged 25 and over under a mandatory permanent-infertility mandate with repeated evaluations at government-approved hospitals; healthcare professionals performing such care would face fines and up to seven years in prison, and trans people receiving deemed-illegal care up to three years, forcing treatment underground. The LGBTI+ association's monitoring report finds that 2025 hostility toward LGBTI+ people became explicit state policy — 'Year of the Family' instructions issued to public institutions, an LGBTI+ association closed with criminal cases against 11 of its members, and artistic events cancelled or banned; the state's blanket bans on LGBTI public events are national practice, not provincial choices.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: Parent-nation policy turbulence: the October 2025 package is a leaked draft, not enacted law; the rights-monitoring organisation Human Rights Watch called it one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades, fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association opposed the draft, and the organisation warns it would force treatment underground and expose people to arrest and pretrial detention. The 2025 monitoring counts — 6 right-to-life violations including 3 hate-motivated killings (trans people the most affected), 89 torture or ill-treatment violations up from 51 the prior year, roughly 313 total violations overall, about 2.5 times the previous year, with 299 detention decisions and freedom-of-expression violations rising from 216 to 540 — are country-wide figures presented as national practice rather than provincial choice, with no provincial breakdown for this province.
rewrites.localsOnly: No province-specific resident data is recorded: no cultural-role, birth-register or resident-discrimination fact for Karabük appears in the record, and the national monitoring counts above are country-wide figures rather than provincial resident statistics.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: The record is national-level and carries no provincial breakdown, so neither a more protective nor a more hostile local regime can be established for this province; the documented national picture applies here unchanged. The October 2025 package is a leaked draft, so its enactment outcome is unresolved. Per the country research dossier, the absence of a documented provincial ban here is not evidence of tolerance, and equally not evidence of a local ban — the national blanket-ban practice applies across the country. No source addresses border-screening or document/identity-check practice for trans visitors to this province, and no marriage or partner-travel information is recorded beyond the ceremony provision above.
